claim: For every finite quiver \(Q=(Q_0,Q_1,s,t)\) and finite field \(k=\mathbb F_q\), let \(J\) be the arrow ideal and \(A=kQ/J^2\). Write \(m_{uv}=|\{\alpha\in Q_1:s(\alpha)=u,\ t(\alpha)=v\}|\), \(E=|Q_1|\), \(L=\sum_{v\in Q_0}m_{vv}\), and \(\Gamma_Q=\{\sigma\in\operatorname{Sym}(Q_0):m_{uv}=m_{\sigma(u)\sigma(v)}\text{ for all }u,v\}\). The map induced on \(A/J\) has image \(\Gamma_Q\), its kernel is isomorphic to \((J/(Z(A)\cap J),+)\rtimes\prod_{u,v\in Q_0}\operatorname{GL}_{m_{uv}}(k)\), and hence \(\left|\operatorname{Aut}_{k\text{-alg}}(A)\right|=q^{E-L}|\Gamma_Q|\prod_{u,v\in Q_0}|\operatorname{GL}_{m_{uv}}(\mathbb F_q)|\), with \(\operatorname{GL}_0(\mathbb F_q)\) trivial.

correctness.rationale: The proof reduces the automorphism count to (i) the vertex-permutation image preserving m_uv, (ii) the subgroup fixing every vertex idempotent, and (iii) inner conjugations by 1+J. The idempotent conjugacy unit u=sum_v phi(e_v)e_v is congruent to 1 modulo J, hence invertible. The vertex-fixing subgroup is exactly the product of GL_{m_uv}; loops are precisely Z(A)∩J, so the inner subgroup has order q^(E-L). The factors intersect trivially, and every kernel automorphism factors as stated. Six exhaustive F_2 checks corroborate the formula, without replacing the symbolic proof.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a uniform automorphism-group kernel decomposition and exact order for every finite split basic radical-square-zero quiver algebra, including disconnected quivers, loops and parallel arrows. The decomposition separates the unipotent inner contribution, each arrow-block linear group, and vertex symmetries; this is a reusable input for automorphism-weighted enumeration and comparison of finite-dimensional algebras, rather than a single small numerical case.
